 Live .  19,277 viewing 19277 viewing Australia need MCG record 188 to beat England in first T20
 Sat 21 Nov 2026 , Men's International Twenty20 Match - 1st T20I Australia (batting) vs England, in play Australia Australia In Play England England 43 -1 ( 5.2 ) 187 -9 ( 20.0 ) Australia need 145 runs to win from 14.4 overs with 9 wickets remaining Australia innings: 43 for 1 from 5.2 overs, in play
 England innings: 187 for 9 from 20.0 overs
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 First of five T20s, Melbourne
 Australia need 188 to win
 England hit record T20 international total at MCG
 Eng 187-9 (20 overs): Brook 65 (28), Banton 39 (22)

 Will Jacks said "that's out" and Mitch Marsh has started walking off.
 But the third umpure shows he's just got a smidgen of bat over the line.

 Brilliant work from Overton at mid-on. Marsh reckons he's gone here.
 26 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Umpire review published at 4.5 overs 4.5 overs 
 Mitch Marsh with a risky single but a smart piece of work from Jamie Overton, who hits the stumps at the non-striker's end with his shy.
 This looks very close.
 20 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 10:24 GMT 10:24 GMT 
 This will be a record chase at the MCG if Australia can reach the target of 188. 
 The highest T20 international score at the ground is the 186-5 made by India against Zimbabwe at the 2022 T20 World Cup.
 12 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 41-1 published at 4.1 overs 4.1 overs 
 Sam Curran into the attack but Mitch Marsh pummels the left-arm seamer straight back down the ground for four.
 That just missed the standing umpire's head.
 2 25 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 37-1 published at 10:22 GMT 10:22 GMT 
 More expensive still from Jamie Overton. 
 The England all-rounder shakes his head after a wild flash of the bat from Sam Harper and an edge goes fine for four.
 A dot to finish from Overton.
 2 37 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 10:20 GMT 10:20 GMT 
 Henry Moeran 
Commentator on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 
 That's clever! It could be six...and it is. Jamie Overton has been expensive here.
 4 28 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 33-1 published at 3.4 overs 3.4 overs 
 A square cut for four from Sam Harper before a majestic shot.
 The Aussie batter throws off any nervousness against Liam Dawson to ramp Jamie Overton for six 
 4 32 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 10:19 GMT 10:19 GMT 
 Henry Moeran 
Commentator on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 
 It was swirling high up and Sam Harper got a little lucky.
 8 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 23-1 published at 3.2 overs 3.2 overs 
 Jamie Overton replaces Henry Crocombe.
 Sam Harper picks up a four before he skies one...but the diving Aneurin Donald cannot quite get there.
 7 27 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 16-1 published at 3 overs 3 overs 
 Not much for Sam Harper to free his arms up with against Liam Dawson, who is a wily canny and operator.
 Harper is able to flick one off his pads for a couple before jabbing a single down the ground to keep the strike,.
 22 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing

 Liam Dawson in the powerplay under Harry Brook in T20 internationals:
 136 runs

 17.00 average

 89 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 13-1 published at 2.1 overs 2.1 overs 
 Sam Harper is the new batter for Australia following the loss of Jake Fraser-McGurk.
 Mitch Marsh bunts Liam Dawson down the ground to get Harper on strike. The England spinner makes a tweak to his field.
 17 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 10:13 GMT 10:13 GMT 
 Darren Lehmann 
Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 Australia have lost early wickets in the last few games, different format obviously. They will want to play with freedom, though, and want to get off to a flyer.
 9 47 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 11-1 published at 2 overs 2 overs 
 Deftly guided by Mitch Marsh through the third region off Henry Crocombe, but Phil Salt makes a tumbling stop to prevent the boundary.
 Scoreboard pressure will be key for England here you feel, particularly with a few green players in this Australia side.
 18 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 10:11 GMT 10:11 GMT 
 Jason Gillespie 
Former Australia bowler on BBC Test Match Special 
 It wasn't that short but that's in Mitchell Marsh's absolute wheelhouse.
 6 36 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 9-1 published at 1.1 overs 1.1 overs 
 Henry Crocombe with the second over. Mitch Marsh gets it short with his first ball and decisively pulls it for six behind square.
